title: The Serpent Eats Itself
author: Troy Nahumko
content:
There is an old and rather useful principle in political philosophy—useful, at
least, to anyone not actively attempting to build a belief system out of fumes
and grievances—that you cannot construct a livable house on a foundation of
pure negation. You can, however, erect something like a haunted shack: all
drafts and whispers, full of imagined enemies, structurally unsound and
permanently one hard knock away from collapse.
